turns.user: how do I do a deadlift
turns.reply:
To do a deadlift, the goal is to pull the bar from the floor to your hips using your glutes, hamstrings, and back, keeping the bar as close to your body as possible. 

Here are the three most important setup cues to focus on:

1. Line up the bar — Stand with your feet hip-width apart, with the barbell directly over the middle of your feet (about an inch away from your shins).
2. Get your grip and set your shins — Bend at the hips and knees to grab the bar just outside your legs, then push your shins forward until they touch the bar without moving it.
3. Flatten your back and pull — Flatten your back by lifting your chest, take a big breath into your stomach, and push the floor away to stand up.

[Watch Barbell Deadlift Tutorial on YouTube](www.youtube.com/results?search_query=barbell+deadlift+tutorial+form)

turns.reply:
Here is the complete breakdown for the deadlift, from your setup to the lift itself. 

The Setup
1. Stance — Stand with your feet hip-width apart. The barbell should cut exactly across the middle of your feet. If you look down, it should be about an inch from your shins.
2. Grip — Hinge at your hips and bend your knees just enough to grab the bar. Your hands should be just outside your legs, with a firm grip.
3. Shins to bar — Without moving the barbell, drop your hips slightly and push your shins forward until they make contact with the bar. 
4. Pack your lats — Imagine trying to squeeze oranges in your armpits. This pulls your shoulders back and down, locking your upper back in place.
5. Set your back and brace — Lift your chest up to flatten your spine. Take a deep breath into your belly, brace your core tight, and pull the slack out of the bar so it clicks.

The Lift
1. Push the floor away — Do not try to yank the bar up with your arms. Think about leg pressing the floor away from you.
2. Bar path — Keep the bar in contact with your shins and thighs the entire way up. It should travel in a straight vertical line.
3. Lockout — Stand tall by squeezing your glutes at the top. Do not lean back or hyperextend your lower back.

The Descent
1. Hinge first — Push your hips back as if trying to touch a wall behind you. Let the bar slide down your thighs.
2. Clear the knees — Once the bar passes your knees, bend your legs to lower the weight back to the floor. Let the weight come to a complete stop before starting your next rep.

[Watch Barbell Deadlift Tutorial on YouTube](www.youtube.com/results?search_query=barbell+deadlift+tutorial+form)
